messages:
deploy-bot: starting canary rollout v2-streaming -> 5% traffic (canary targets: canary-1, canary-2, canary-3). rolling out model: rwd-stream-v2-quant. watch: /integrations/canary/1781234567
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: canary-3 elevated 5xx rate 6.8% (1m) — healthcheck failures 3/5 in last 2m. abort-criteria: 5xx > 3% for 5m OR 3 consecutive hc failures. paging @maria @aj oncall.
maria: ack. oncall here. paging @aj @kevin — canary-3 looks noisy. starting triage.
aj: pulling logs now, attaching recent pod logs from canary-3. running: `kubectl -n prod logs deploy/streaming-canary-3 --tail=500`
aj: logs excerpt:
```
Error: WorkerOOM - failed to allocate 2.0G GPU memory
  at Transformer.forward (model/transformer.py:421)
  at Runner.generate (runtime/gpu_runner.cpp:113)
Caused by: CUDA out of memory
```
aj: also seeing repeated 502/504 upstreams from the redis KV cache layer, and our rate-limiter for streaming is queuing.
kevin: interesting — we pushed a different quantization knob for rwd-stream-v2-quant in this rollout. could be memory profile mismatch causing OOM + backpressure.
sam: product-ops — any signs of customer-facing errors? how many requests are impacted?
maria: quick stats from dashboard: ~4.2k requests in last 5m for canary slice, 5xx count ~290 (6.9%). A small set of EU accounts are seeing failure rates ~12% for streaming endpoints. not widespread but visible for live sessions.
aj: given the OOMs and redis timeouts, i'd prefer to flip the feature flag for streaming_v2 to route users off the new code path while we investigate. we can also pause the rollout and scale down canary pods.
product-ops: +1 on kill-switch. customers impacted include a beta cohort (beta-streaming). need ETA for mitigation before we message them.
maria: agreed. aj — can you flip the ff and then run abort? i want canary paused and traffic routed to legacy streaming path.
aj: executing flag toggle now:
```
$ ffctl set streaming_v2 false --env=prod --scope=canary --actor=aj --reason="canary 5xx spike / OOM"
ffctl-bot: feature flag streaming_v2 set to false for scope=canary by aj
```
aj: triggering canary abort: `deploy-bot abort --canary canary-3 --reason "healthcheck failures / 5xx spike"`
deploy-bot: canary abort initiated for canary-3. scaling down canary pods, shifting traffic back to baseline model. pause further rollout.
incident-bot: monitor: 5xx rate for canary slice dropping — previous 6.8% -> current 0.9% (2m after flag flip). healthchecks returning to green.
kevin: seeing memory usage normalize on nodes tied to canary-3; no further OOM traces in last 90s. looks like the new quantization path causes increased GPU allocation under concurrent streaming workloads.
maria: good. product-ops, recommend holding customer-facing status until we confirm stable for 15m. if stable, we can send an interim note describing degraded streaming for beta users and action taken.
product-ops: will draft a short status. ETA 10m. include that we paused rollout and routed affected users to legacy path; remediation ongoing.
aj: creating incident ticket and adding initial notes + logs: INC-17812. adding action items: revert quant knob in model compile, add memory guardrail, add canary-specific mem limit.
maria: handing off remaining monitoring and post-incident ops to kevin for the rest of the oncall window. kevin — you have the handoff. please escalate to infra if we see any regression.
kevin: got it. taking over oncall. I'll keep the incident bridge open and run an extended monitoring query for 30m.
incident-bot: oncall handoff recorded: from maria -> kevin at 2026-03-15T18:00:10Z (thread_ts 1781234567).
maria: thanks team :white_check_mark: — closing immediate mitigation. follow-ups: (1) root cause triage with model team (aj + kevin), (2) add automatic canary mem-sentinel, (3) customer comms draft by product-ops.
product-ops: ack — drafting now.
aj: I'll also pin a rollback PR to prevent accidental re-rollout until we have fixes.
kevin: leaving logs and a short runbook in the incident ticket. ping me if 5xx creeps up again.
maria: marking this thread as resolved for immediate paging, leaving incident ticket open for postmortem. handoff done. :lock:
